title: Redwood October 2026 All-Hands
topics: Product updates: Redwood API, Console, Optimize
summary: Company all-hands covering Q3 results, Q4 roadmap with focus on Dedicated and Private deployments, product updates across API/Console/Optimize, hiring plans, and security/compliance milestones. Leadership recapped customer successes and outlined next steps for org priorities and sales enablement.
action_items: Priya Nair: Publish Q4 roadmap doc and send to company (due 2026-10-13)
Marco Alvarez: Share dedicated capacity benchmark summary and kernel optimization notes (due 2026-10-20)
Luis Ortega: Kick off two cross-team reliability drills and share findings (due 2026-11-01)
Jasmine Lee: Post updated hiring comp bands and recruiting funnel status (due 2026-10-08)
Sales Ops: Create playbook for Dedicated + Private upsell with case studies (due 2026-10-22)
next_steps: Roadmap doc distributed and AMA with Product next week
SEs to get Dedicated benchmark spreadsheet and run with top 5 pilot accounts
Security to publish SOC2 Type II audit timeline and FAQ for customers
People Ops to host hiring town hall with engineering managers
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-10-06 | Start: 10:00 AM PT | Duration approx 1:15 | Location: Virtual All-hands (Zoom)
Attendees: Sara (CEO), Marco (CTO), Priya (Head of Product), Luis (VP Eng), Jasmine (Head of People), ~220 employees

00:00 Sara Kim: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining, um let's get started. Quick housekeeping, the recording will be posted, and notes will be in the all-hands channel.
00:18 Sara Kim: First slide, high level Q3 recap — strong growth across hosted API usage, a good set of Dedicated deals closed and a few Private engagements in final negotiation. I want to thank the sales and infra teams, uh it's been a huge push.
00:42 Marco Alvarez: Just to add on infra, latency improvements from the kernel work gave us about 12-18% lower p99 on our standard long-context models, so that's showing up in demos and benchmarks. There's still more to squeeze out.
01:05 Priya Nair: On product, Q3 we shipped streaming function support and structured output templates for the API, and the Console rollout for route-level analytics is now GA. Early feedback: customers love the token breakdown per route.
01:28 Employee (Engineering): Quick question, is the Console analytics retained how long by default?
01:33 Priya Nair: Uh default retention is 30 days for the free tier, enterprise can opt for longer retention as an add-on. We'll put a doc in the channel.
01:49 Luis Ortega: On reliability, we had two incident windows in Q3, both mitigated with automated fallback to smaller model variants, but lesson learned is we need better orchestration for cross-region fallbacks.
02:10 Marco Alvarez: Right, and the smart routing logic will get an update to consider capacity tier and latency SLO before switching model variants, that should reduce churning.
02:33 Sara Kim: Customer wins — shout out to HorizonPay and AtlasHealth who both went live with Dedicated capacity. HorizonPay's case is nice because they needed PCI adjacency and VPC peering.
02:56 Employee (Sales): Any notes on pricing concessions for those deals?
03:03 Sara Kim: We did one-time onboarding credit in both cases, and structured ramp discounts tied to usage commitments. Sales ops will pack that into the playbook.
03:20 Priya Nair: Moving into Q4 priorities — three big bets: 1) Dedicated capacity scale and smoother on-boarding experience, 2) Private (VPC/on-prem) productization for regulated verticals, 3) Redwood Optimize features to help customers reduce per-token costs via quantization suggestions and caching.
03:46 Marco Alvarez: For Dedicated scale, kernel selection is key. We're also working on continuous batching improvements and smarter KV cache eviction so models with long contexts don't blow memory.
04:05 Employee (Product): You said KV cache, last update it was spelled out as KV cash in some demos, is that still the same? [laughs]
04:12 Marco Alvarez: [laughs] yes KV cache, not cash. The transcript generator likes dollar signs apparently.
04:24 Jasmine Lee: Quick HR update: we hired 34 people in Q3, need to keep ramping, our biggest gaps are infra SRE and solutions engineers for Dedicated onboarding. We'll be posting reqs this week.
04:46 Employee (Engineering): Any update on comp bands?
04:50 Jasmine Lee: Yes, comp bands are being updated; I'll put the new ranges in Workday and host a Q&A. Also we are piloting a flex office days policy for SF and NY teams.
05:08 Sara Kim: Security & compliance — we've completed the SOC2 Type II readiness audit and the audit firm is scheduling the final review for late October, this should make us fully SOC2 Type II certified early November assuming no surprises. We also ongoingly support ISO prep for selected customers.
05:37 Employee (Customer Success): For the Private deployments, what's the ETA for the on-prem orchestration docs?
05:43 Priya Nair: Docs are in draft, we'll publish a runbook and a reference architecture by mid-October. SEs will get a hardened checklist for pilot deployments.
06:01 Marco Alvarez: Technical deep dive highlight — we prototyped a quantized kernel path that runs at 4-bit and shows minimal quality regression on our eval sets for classification tasks, great for cost-sensitive production workloads. We'll put the benchmark spreadsheet in the se-team channel.
06:31 Employee (SWE): Are we planning to open-source any of the kernel work?
06:36 Marco Alvarez: Not yet; parts may be open sourced after we clean up IP and doc it, but a lot is tuning for our runtime.
06:46 Priya Nair: Customer feedback loops — we launched evals tied to prompt sets and regression alerts. This caught two regressions caused by model updates last month before customers noticed. Big win for the team.
07:10 Sara Kim: OK quick financials — total ARR growth quarter-over-quarter was 28%, gross margin improved slightly due to higher utilization of Dedicated slots and caching. Net burn is down on a rate basis; our plan is to keep runway healthy while investing in Dedicated and Private sales motion.
07:39 Employee (Finance): Any changes to pricing or packaging?
07:42 Sara Kim: No immediate changes; we'll refine packaging for Dedicated with clearer commit tiers and burst options.
07:53 Employee (Support): On retention/engagement, anything new for the Console to help health signals?
07:58 Priya Nair: Yes health dashboards and a per-route SLA indicator coming in the next release.
08:08 Luis Ortega: Engineering priorities for the next 90 days: finish the reliability automation, reduce p99 for long-context models by another 10%, and ship the private deployment orchestrator alpha. We'll post the sprint objectives.
08:30 Employee (PM): Any dependency on cloud partners for Private orchestration?
08:36 Luis Ortega: We're supporting AWS and GCP in alpha; later we'll add Azure depending on demand.
08:44 Sara Kim: Customer stories — short highlights: AtlasHealth replaced a legacy reranker and cut inference costs by 40% with our batching and caching config; HorizonPay used on-prem pilot to meet compliance while maintaining latency SLO. These will be in the playbook.
09:10 Open Q&A segment begins
09:15 Employee (Engineering): Can we get more clarity on who to contact for pilot accounts?
09:20 Sales Ops: Use pilot-hosting@redwood.com and cc the AE and SE, we'll triage.
09:30 Employee (Customer Success): How are we measuring success for the Dedicated upsell motion?
09:36 Sara Kim: Primary metrics: committed ARR from Dedicated, time-to-value for pilot (target <6 weeks), and churn rate for Dedicated customers.
09:50 Employee (Intern): Are there opportunities for interns to contribute to kernel testing?
09:54 Marco Alvarez: Definitely, we'll set up a rotation for interns to run experiments against our benchmark harness.
10:04 Jasmine Lee: Reminder—eng managers should submit hiring prioritization spreadsheets by Friday.
10:12 Sara Kim: Last note — thanks team, big quarter, but lots to do. We'll recap in the all-hands notes and there will be an AMA with Priya and Marco next Tuesday.
10:28 Crowd: [applause emoji in chat] [crosstalk]
10:40 Sara Kim: Alright, meeting adjourned.

Recap (verbatim): Q3 strong growth, Dedicated & Private are top GTM pushes for Q4, product is shipping Console analytics + Optimize improvements, security near SOC2 Type II, hiring continues focused on infra and SE, action items assigned.
